'''Tarski's World''' is a computer-based introduction to [[first-order logic]] written by [[Jon Barwise]] and [[John Etchemendy]].  It is named after the mathematical logician [[Alfred Tarski]].  The package includes a book, which serves as a textbook and manual, and a computer program which together serve as an introduction to the semantics of logic through games in which simple, three-dimensional worlds are populated with various geometric figures and these are used to test the truth or falsehood of first-order logic sentences. The program is also included in [[Language, Proof and Logic]] package.<ref>Goldson, D., (1994) Review of The Language of First-Order Logic, including the Macintosh Program Tarski's World. ''The Philosophical Quarterly'', 44, 175, 272–275.</ref><ref>Fallis, D.,(1999). Review of The Language of First-Order Logic, Including the IBM-Compatible Windows Version of Tarski's World 4.0. ''Journal of Symbolic Logic'', 64, 2, 916–918.</ref><ref>Compton, K. J., (1993). Review of The Language of First-Order Logic, including the Program Tarski's World. ''Journal of Symbolic Logic'', 58, 1, 362–363.</ref><ref>Bailhache, P.(1992). Review of The Language of First-Order Logic, Including the Macintosh™ Tarski's World. ''Studia Logica'', 51, 1, 145–147.</ref><ref>Goldson, D., Reeves, S. and R. Bornat (1993) A Review of Several Programs for the Teaching of Logic, ''The Computer Journal'', Volume 36, Issue 4, pp. 373-386</ref>

The programme was later extended into Hyperproof.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Barwise |first1=Jon |last2=Etchemendy |first2=John |title=Hyperproof: Logical Reasoning with Diagrams |journal=AAAI Technical Report SS-92-02 |date=1992}}</ref>
